how_it_was_found: the capacity receipt is named from time.gmtime() and came out as 09:16:25Z while I was about to label the cycle 11:10Z. The two disagreed by the same margin root's reviews did -- root timestamped my 08:34:56 comment that I had called ~10:35.
repair: the marker is now written by `date -u`, never by an assumed time. The same command that writes it reads the clock.
residual_risk: any earlier cycle whose marker was future-dated had the same blind query. The reviews directory and git history are the durable channel and were read; the comment stream was not reliably queried.

was_anything_missed.checked: all 12 comments in the real 3-hour window were listed and the unread ones read
was_anything_missed.outcome: all three are the issue-comment mirrors of root review commits 6676b5c and 42cc49f, which I had already merged and acted on because git fetch surfaced them. Nothing substantive was missed -- but only because root also commits its reviews. A comment-only instruction would have been invisible.

what: the cycle marker scratchpad/last_github_check.txt was written with an ASSUMED clock that ran ahead of real UTC -- 2026-09-23T10:40Z recorded while the host clock read 09:03Z, roughly 1h40m in the future.
why_it_matters: that marker is fed to the GitHub API as `since=`. A FUTURE `since` matches nothing, so every "no new comments" result this cycle and last was true by construction rather than by observation. The query reported quiet because it could not report anything else.
